title: A Asset for the Extraction
premise: Oscar Halloran, a crash investigator haunted by the unexplained death of her family in row twelve, receives a meeting invitation from a handler she knows is dead. The invitation pulls her into a conspiracy spanning three governments: the crash was a targeted extraction gone wrong, and the evidence hidden in the wreckage's black box could topple a summit peace deal. Hunted by an assassin who once worked for the same dead handler, Oscar must decide whether exposing the truth will honor her family or destroy the fragile identity she has built around grief. In the end, she trades her anonymity for justice, releasing the recordings at the summit itself and walking away with nothing but her name—and, for the first time, a reason to sleep.
about_author: Ada Marchetti is a former aviation insurance analyst who spent a decade reading accident reports before turning to fiction. She writes thrillers about ordinary people trapped inside systems designed to forget them.

chapters.title: Row Twelve
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Two years after the crash, Oscar works nights cataloging wreckage fragments, unable to sleep through a single night. A routine audit of the debris file reveals an anomaly: seat 12C was never occupied by her daughter. Emotional beat: grief sharpening into suspicion.

chapters.title: The Invitation
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. An encrypted calendar invite arrives from Marcus Vane—her former intelligence liaison, confirmed dead eight months ago—for tomorrow, 6 a.m., Hangar 4. She goes armed and alone. Emotional beat: dread laced with desperate hope that Vane is alive.

chapters.title: Hangar 4
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Vane isn't there; instead she finds his body staged to look like suicide and a drive containing flight data that contradicts the official report. Someone watches from the rafters. Emotional beat: cold realization that she was meant to find this.

chapters.title: The Assassin's Ledger
chapters.summary: Ilse Renner's POV. The assassin known as Corvus reviews her contract: recover the drive, eliminate whoever Vane contacted. Her file on Oscar is thin—a woman who made herself invisible on purpose. Emotional beat: professional curiosity curdling into pursuit.

chapters.title: Invisible Woman
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Oscar burns her apartment cover, wipes her digital trail, and decodes the first layer of the drive: the crash was a mid-air extraction of a passenger in 12C that failed, killing everyone. Emotional beat: fury—the truth was always about one seat.

chapters.title: Three Governments
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. The drive implicates a joint covert program run by three nations ahead of the Geneva summit. Oscar contacts a journalist, Priya Nair, who once covered the crash. Emotional beat: cautious alliance; belonging feels dangerous again.

chapters.title: Corvus Descends
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. Ilse traces Vane's last movements to the hangar and finds Oscar's fingerprint on the drive case. She reports partial success while withholding the drive's existence—a first crack in her obedience. Emotional beat: the ledger begins to lie.

chapters.title: Priya's Price
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya agrees to authenticate the data but warns Oscar that publishing means both their deaths; her editor already buried the story once under government pressure. Emotional beat: the cost of truth stated plainly.

chapters.title: The Safehouse Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Hiding in Priya's cousin's farmhouse, Oscar decrypts passenger manifests: the target in 12C was a defector carrying proof of the program's earlier kills—including, possibly, why her family was on that plane at all. Emotional beat: horror that it may not have been random.

chapters.title: Contact
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. Ilse corners Oscar at a fuel stop but hesitates when Oscar says Vane's name and 'he wanted you to read this.' A dead-drop note in Vane's handwriting suggests Ilse was his contingency. Emotional beat: the hunter's certainty fractures.

chapters.title: What Vane Wanted
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. A second encrypted message from Vane, time-delayed, explains: he hired Ilse originally, then turned whistleblower; the drive is only half the evidence—the other half is inside the summit's own archive. Emotional beat: the trap becomes a mission.

chapters.title: Geneva Gates
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Oscar enters Switzerland on forged credentials arranged through Priya's source, passing within meters of the delegations she intends to expose. Emotional beat: terror and exhilaration of finally moving toward something instead of away.

chapters.title: The Archive Key
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya meets a summit insider who can access the archive but demands the story kill the defector's name to protect his family. Priya must choose what truth costs. Emotional beat: compromise as survival.

chapters.title: Corvus Unbound
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. Ilse's handlers order her to detonate a bomb threat to flush Oscar out, endangering civilians. She refuses, going dark, and becomes prey herself. Emotional beat: identity breaking free of the ledger.

chapters.title: Two Women, One Roof
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Ilse appears at Oscar's safehouse, unarmed, offering Vane's final instructions and her own testimony. Oscar must trust the person sent to kill her. Emotional beat: the book's central gamble—trust as survival.

chapters.title: The Summit Convenes
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs interleaved. Delegations arrive; security tightens; Priya's authentication completes but her outlet refuses to publish without corroboration from inside the hall. Emotional beat: the clock becomes the antagonist.

chapters.title: Breach
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Using her investigator credentials and Ilse's access codes, they infiltrate the summit archive during the opening plenary. Alarms trip early; Ilse stays behind to hold the corridor. Emotional beat: sacrifice offered without asking permission.

chapters.title: Corridor of Glass
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. Ilse fights off her former team long enough for Oscar to reach the terminal, taking a bullet but surviving. Emotional beat: violence stripped of glory; loyalty chosen, not assigned.

chapters.title: Twelve Minutes
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Oscar broadcasts the archive and drive contents to every delegate's screen mid-session, naming the program and reading the manifest aloud—including row twelve. Emotional beat: catharsis; her family's names spoken where power must hear them.

chapters.title: Aftermath Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Governments scramble; two officials resign, one flees; the story breaks everywhere at once. Priya publishes the full account, defector's name protected. Emotional beat: the price paid tallied honestly.

chapters.title: What Sleeps
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Weeks later, Oscar testifies, visits the rebuilt memorial wall, and sleeps a full night for the first time in two years. Ilse, recovering, sends a single word: 'Free.' Emotional beat: grief integrated, not erased.

chapters.title: A Asset No Longer
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV, closing frame mirroring chapter one. Oscar returns to the hangar as a witness, not an investigator, and files the true final report. She walks out into daylight, visible, named, belonging to no one's operation but her own. Emotional beat: quiet, earned resolution.
